column1: # Names a harness already gives its own maintained capability. No skill in this repository may
# reuse one: validate.sh fails the build on a match, and doctor.sh reports a match on the installed
# checkout. Tab-separated: harness, kind, name, version the entry was verified on.
# Why a hand-kept list: neither harness offers a stable interface a script can query for its
# bundled names. Claude Code compiles its bundled skills into the binary and materializes them
# lazily, so no directory ever holds the full set. Codex keeps its system skills on disk under
# $CODEX_HOME/skills/.system, which doctor.sh reads live on top of this list. A release can add a
# name this list lacks; refresh it against each new harness version:
#   Claude Code  run /skills or /context in a session; every entry whose source is "Built-in" is
#                bundled. The documented precedence (code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) is that a
#                personal or project skill replaces a bundled one of the same name but not its
#                aliases, so aliases are listed too.
# kind: skill (bundled skill), alias (a bundled skill's alias), reserved (a name the harness
# refuses for user skills), system-skill (Codex system skill).
